newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX noon Nikkei futures up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX noon Nikkei futures up on short-covering.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures were firmer at midday on Tuesday following a bout of active short-covering after recent falls, dealers said.
Japanese trading houses and arbitrageuers were the main buyers while western brokerages were sellers, they said.
"There was no particular news that prompted the renewed buying, just short-covering since the market doesn't look as if it would fall much further," said a dealer with a Japanese institution.
At 0235 GMT, the Nikkei September futures were up 170 points at 19,930. Volume was at 7,555 lots.
Dealers said the sentiment was cautious with near-term direction unclear.
The dollar's move above 113 yen after Japan's Ministry of Finance Eisuke Sakakibara said there had been no change in the foreign exchange policy was largely shrugged off in Singapore.
"Dollar/yen is still trading within a range of 113/115. So, there is not much of a reaction here," said the dealer.
Resistance for September Nikkei was seen at 19,975-20,000.
